themes_detail.label: Street Deterioration Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 82 THIS WEEK, up 277% from the 8-week average of 21.8 complaints per week—a statistically significant surge (z-score: 8.26) suggesting either rapid pavement failure or deferred maintenance across Forest Hills/Rego Park.
evidence: 82 street condition complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 21.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (277% spike)
Z-score of 8.26 indicates statistically extreme deviation from baseline
Street Condition ranks 5th in all 311 complaint categories for the district over 90 days (655 total complaints)
reporting_angles: Canvass multiple blocks in Rego Park and Forest Hills to document specific potholes, crumbling curbs, and subsurface damage; interview residents about hazards to vehicles and pedestrians
Contact NYC DOT to determine if this is reactive reporting of existing damage or if deterioration accelerated; request work orders filed this week vs. prior weeks

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Surge in Residential Areas
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints jumped to 5 THIS WEEK, a 900% increase from the 8-week average of 0.5 complaints per week (z-score: 6.36)—indicating either a new tagging campaign or organized vandalism affecting the neighborhood.
evidence: 5 graffiti complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (900% spike)
Z-score of 6.36 indicates statistically extreme outlier
No prior graffiti spike in 90-day data suggests this is new phenomenon
reporting_angles: Visit complaint locations to photograph tags and identify whether they share crew names, symbols, or style; document if they're gang-related or copycat vandalism
Interview NYPD Community Affairs about whether they've detected a tagging crew or gang activity increase this week; check if arrests correlate

themes_detail.label: Dangling Street Signs Pose Safety Hazard
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about dangling street signs surged to 9 LAST WEEK, up 380% from the 8-week average of 1.9 per week (z-score: 4.04)—a potential public safety risk if signs are falling or obscuring traffic information.
evidence: 9 dangling street sign complaints filed LAST WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (380% spike)
Z-score of 4.04 indicates statistically significant outlier
Traffic Signal Condition is also elevated (378 complaints over 90 days), suggesting broader signage/infrastructure decay
reporting_angles: Walk major intersections (Yellowstone Boulevard, Queens Boulevard, 108th Street) to identify loose or dangling signs; photograph hazards and confirm if they obstruct driver sight lines
Request NYC DOT maintenance records for this district to determine if sign repairs were deferred or if weather damage (wind, ice) caused sudden failures

themes_detail.label: Appliance-Related Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Appliance complaints (likely heating/cooking equipment failures in rent-stabilized buildings) jumped to 5 LAST WEEK, up 264% from the 8-week average of 1.4 per week (z-score: 4.23)—suggesting potential building code violations or landlord neglect.
evidence: 5 appliance complaints filed LAST WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (264% spike)
Z-score of 4.23 indicates statistically significant deviation
Heat/Hot Water complaints are highest-volume category across district (2076 complaints over 90 days), suggesting systematic landlord neglect
reporting_angles: Contact HPD to cross-reference recent appliance complaints with housing violations; determine if specific buildings appear in multiple complaints
Interview tenants to learn whether complaints are for stoves, ovens, or water heaters; identify any pattern of non-response from landlords

themes_detail.label: Dead Trees and Green Infrastructure Decline
themes_detail.summary: Dead/dying tree complaints jumped to 3 LAST WEEK, a 700% spike from the 8-week average of 0.4 per week (z-score: 3.77)—indicating potential disease, pest infestation, or city forestry service failure in a district with repeated budget requests for park/greenspace.
evidence: 3 dead/dying tree complaints filed LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike)
Z-score of 3.77 indicates statistically significant outlier
Community Board has repeatedly requested funding for new/expanded parks and greenspace amenities, suggesting long-standing tree/landscaping neglect
reporting_angles: Visit parks and street tree zones (especially along Yellowstone Boulevard and Queens Boulevard) to document disease, pest damage, or maintenance failure; photograph dead trees
Contact NYC Parks to determine if budget cuts or staffing shortages have reduced tree maintenance; cross-check with prior tree disease outbreaks in Queens
